key_insight: Self-powered microsystems will likely require hybrid energy harvesting plus better power management, because no single ambient source or storage device is yet sufficient for reliable long-term operation.
engineering_relevance: For IoT, wearables, and cyber-physical devices, the main design challenge is system-level integration of harvesters, PMICs, and storage under real-world low-power and variable-input conditions.
method: Surveyed triboelectric, piezoelectric/pyroelectric, indoor photovoltaic, and RF rectenna harvesters
Highlighted hybrid multi-source architectures and metamaterial-enabled broadband RF designs
Reviewed low-voltage cold-start PMICs, impedance matching, and storage degradation as deployment bottlenecks
evidence_signal: The abstract reports specific performance advances such as over 300% wider operational bandwidth for nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators and emphasizes recent breakthroughs in materials and RF harvesting architectures.
watch_item: Promising lab-scale gains may not translate directly to field reliability because cold-start limits, source mismatch, and micro-supercapacitor or thin-film battery degradation remain unresolved.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
